speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI results indicate demyelinating lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) caused by JC virus, likely in the context of immunosuppression; the patient's claim of multiple sclerosis is incorrect. Can you describe any recent severe infections, chemotherapy, or use of immunosuppressive medications? Additionally, have you experienced any visual disturbances, weakness, or changes in speech?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the MRI findings of PML lesions and your history of ataxia, we need to confirm the underlying cause of your immunosuppression. Have you been diagnosed with HIV/AIDS, or have you recently undergone chemotherapy or taken medications like rituximab or natalizumab? Additionally, have you noticed any recent vision loss, weakness in your limbs, or changes in your speech?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy in a patient with Crohn's disease.
